chunks: Tamim ibn Abdullah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi narrated that his father told him, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, who said: I said to Ar-Rida (peace be upon him),

"There are people in the vicinity of Kufa who claim that the Prophet did not make any mistake in his prayer." He said, "They lie, may God curse them. The One who does not make a mistake is God, the One there is no god but He."

I said, "O son of the Messenger of God! Among them are people who claim that Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was not killed, and that his likeness was thrown onto Hanzala ibn As'ad al-Shami, and that he was raised to the sky just as Jesus ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) was raised." And they use this verse as proof: "And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way over the believers."
And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way over the believers.

He said, "They lie, upon them be the wrath and curse of God! They disbelieved by denying the Messenger of God when he informed that Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) would be killed. By God, Al-Husayn has been killed, and those better than Al-Husayn were killed: the Commander of the Faithful and Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him). And none of us is except one who will be killed. And I, by God, will be killed by poison by the assassination of one who assassinates me. I know this from a trusted covenant from the Messenger of God, which Gabriel informed him of, from the Lord of the Worlds."

As for the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic, 'And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way over the believers,' then it means He will not grant to an unbeliever against a believer any proof. And God informed, the Mighty and Majestic, that some unbelievers killed the prophets unjustly, and despite their killing them, God did not grant them a way over His prophets in terms of proof.
I have recorded what was narrated on this meaning in the book 'Refutation of the Exaggerators and Those Who Believe in Turning Over the Affairs'.

key_terms.التَّفْوِيضِ: Turning over affairs (referring to Mufawidha sect)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ar-Rida interpret the verse 'And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way over the believers' in the context of the martyrdom of Al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) refutes the Ghulat's claim of the Prophet's infallibility from minor errors (sahw) and their assertion that Al-Husayn was raised to heaven, clarifying that the Quranic verse 'And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way over the believers' (4:141) refers to divine proof (hujjah) rather than physical survival. He affirms the martyrdom of all Imams, including himself, citing the covenant of Gabriel, and notes that this hadith was recorded in his work *Ibtil al-Ghulat* to distinguish between exaggeration and authentic Shia belief.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 46-5 Tamim ibn Abdullah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi - may God have Mercy upon him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Ali Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abi Salt al-Harawi that he told Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.), “O son of the Prophet of God!

There are people in the vicinity of Kufa who think that the Prophet (S) never made any mistakes when saying his prayers.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “May God damn them! They lie. The Only One who makes no mistakes is God - the One and Only.” Abi Salt al-Harawi added, “O son of the Prophet of God!
There are people among them who think that Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) was not killed and God made someone else called Handhala ibn As’ad ash-Shami look like him (and be killed).

And He raised Jesus (a.s.) - the son of (the Blessed Lady) Mary (a.s.) and the reason they present is by using the following verse, ‘…And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way (to triumphs)over the believers.’” The Imam (a.s.) replied, “They are lying.

God’s Wrath and Curse be upon them! They have disbelieved in God by denying what the Prophet (S) has said about Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) being killed, ‘I swear by God that Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) will be killed.’ There is no doubt that Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) has been killed. Even the ones better than Al-Husayn ibn Ali (a.s.) - that is (Ali) the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) and Al-Hassan ibn Ali (a.s.) were killed. There is no one of us who does not get killed. I swear by God that I will also be killed by being poisoned by a tricky unmanly person. I know this from the Trusted Covenant which we have inherited from God’s Prophet (S) that Gabriel delivered to him (a.s.) on behalf of the Lord of the Two Worlds.

And the verse stated by the Honorable the Exalted God, ‘…And never will God grant to the unbelievers a way (to triumphs) over the believers’ provides the proof. This means that God has not granted the unbelievers any proofs superior to those of the believers. There is no doubt that the Honorable the Exalted God has informed us that the unbelievers have unrightfully killed the Divine Prophets without having any proofs or reasons.

Thus God has not left any ways for them to have any proofs against His Prophets (a.s.).”The author of this book (Sheikh al-Sadooq) said, “I have recorded whatever has been narrated on the subjects of exaggerators and those who believe in turning over the affairs in the book Ibtal al-Ghuluw wal Tafweedh.”
